topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate danger signals and molecular recognition criteria
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the molecular signatures of infection and cellular damage used by the innate immune system to identify non-self threats.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic nature, subcellular localization, receptor families, and signaling cascades that process innate danger signals.

topics.label: Inflammatory cascade, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sentinel cell activation coordinates local leukocyte extravasation, lymphatic priming of adaptive immunity, and potentially fatal systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms that shut down acute inflammation, mediate tissue repair, and contain persistent unresolved stimuli through granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and announces the subject of the next lecture.
